title: The emancipation centennial show and the cast album after Kennedy's assassination
summary: The show celebrated a century of Negro progress; the cast album was recorded after November 1963 with the same company.

story.theme_name: Duke Ellington and his orchestra, as others knew them
story.community_name: Duke Ellington: the band, the man, his men

blocks.x: That was a celebration of a centennial of Negro progress.
It was 100 years since the Emancipation Proclamation.
In fact President Kennedy had -- I think he was responsible for a lot of that at that point, you know.
Because after we finished the engagement in Chicago and the President was assassinated, we had to go back to do a cast album, you know, that was after November.
Oh, I don't think I knew that that was done after the assassination.
Oh, yes, it was done after the assassination, because everybody was depressed about, you know, shaken up with Kennedy's death. And we went back and we got it off the ground okay.
You got everybody that was on the show, the same band?
Yes, we did. The same band and the choir, Bunny Briggs. Let's see, did we get Joya?
Yeah. And Lil Greenwood and Jimmy
Yeah, we did. We were able to collect everybody again.
